answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all 9 II and deal 5 face down above them; shuffle all 3 I and deal 1 face down on top. Return the unused I and II cards unseen to the box.
answers.evidence: Setup: face-down 10-card Conflict Deck; return unused cards without looking.

answers.answer: In four-player play, each human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play, each starts at 0 VP. In both, each gets 2 Agents on their Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, 3 troops in their garrison and 9 in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: Score track 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader; three garrison troops, nine supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn with Agents left; after Revealing, you are skipped for the rest of Player Turns and cannot take a later Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards left in hand and revealed for that Reveal turn, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, move every card in front of you from both types of turns to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Agent turns optional; after Reveal your turns are skipped. Reveal Turn: effects of just-revealed cards only; Clean Up moves all cards in front to discard.

answers.answer: A Plot Intrigue played during your own Agent turn may grant resources before placement, and those resources may pay that visit’s entry cost. Resources from the played Agent card or destination effects occur after placement and cannot pay that entry cost. One card can send only one Agent, using one matching Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played for an Agent turn; it can only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot resources before placement join available supply; later gains cannot pay same entry. Agent Turn: one icon/one Agent; no-icon card only Reveal.

answers.answer: Deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus at most 2 of the 4 troops already in your garrison, for up to 5. At a non-Combat space, normal deployment is not allowed. Recruited troops are taken from your supply and placed in your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: deploy any/all units recruited this turn plus up to two more from garrison, at a Combat space; cube recruits from supply into garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon on the played card allows the Agent to go to any space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; that Spy stays there. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent on that destination; it cannot bypass your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card when you send an Agent, chosen immediately after placing the Agent and before any space/card effects. You cannot use the same Spy for both; on one placement you may use different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather Intelligence timing and distinct Spy restrictions.

answers.answer: Strength is 2×2 troop + 1×3 sandworm + 4 swords = 11. If your last unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot play Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: troops 2 each, sandworms 3, swords 1; last unit removed means 0. Intrigue cards: Combat only if at least one unit deployed.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you acting again if an opponent plays; the Combat Intrigue window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to each player’s supply, Combat markers reset to 0, and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: players may play or pass; not required to pass after earlier pass; consecutive passes close. Cleanup returns troops, resets markers, returns worms.

answers.answer: With exactly two tied for first in a four-player Conflict, each tied player gets the second reward; the other two compete for the third reward. No one wins the Conflict and nobody takes its card. In a three-player Conflict, the two tied first each get second reward, no other reward is given, and nobody takes the card. A zero-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first with 4 players leaves others competing for third; 3 or fewer give no other rewards. Strength/rewards: zero strength no reward.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles your rewards once; multiple worms do not multiply it again. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice once for 1 VP, or pay 6 spice to take it twice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms double; control and battle icons cannot; optional cost may be paid again (3 spice example).

answers.answer: After winning and taking a Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against your other face-up Conflict or Objective cards. Matching is mandatory: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild battle icon may match any one of the three icon types in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: winner takes card, check matching face-up Conflict or Objective; must flip pair; Endgame wild match.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; you lose that VP below 2 and regain it on reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first to 4 also gains the Alliance token and 1 VP; that VP follows token possession. Tying the holder does not steal it: a challenger must rise above the holder. If the holder loses Influence while previously tied, FAQ transfer rules apply.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Faction Influence: 2 VP reversal; 4 track bonus retained; Alliance token temporary VP; tying does not transfer.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, Persuasion can be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one purchase and split one source across several purchases. The Imperium Row is replenished to five, so you may buy the replacement immediately if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal timing, pool/split, replace missing Row cards, acquired card enters discard.

answers.answer: At Makers, put 1 spice in each Maker space with no Agent, adding to existing bonus spice; a visitor gains all bonus spice there. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Sandworms cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while Shield Wall remains; removing it permits worms at any Conflict. Hooks are only required where the effect specifies them, and are retained rather than spent. A worm goes directly to your Conflict, never your garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers; Sandworms; Board Space Guide entries for Deep Desert and Hagga Basin.

answers.answer: At Recall, after the round, 10+ VP by any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. First, players may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues; then compare VP. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then troops in garrison.
answers.evidence: Recall phase and Scoring: endgame trigger at end of a round; Endgame Intrigue before winner; ordered tiebreakers.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup exposes 2 face-up contract offers and puts the remaining 18 standard tokens face down in the bank. Shuffle 4 additional Intrigue cards into that deck and 4 additional Imperium cards into that deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are left in the box and are not part of standard setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes: 20 contracts shuffled, two offers, 18 bank; add 4 cards each; Shaddam optional. Contrasting-back set excluded.

answers.answer: With CHOAM and available contracts, the icon lets you take one face-up contract and replace it with a face-up token from the bank; without CHOAM, or when all contracts have been taken by players, it gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes when an Agent visits a Maker space and the player gains the stated total spice that turn, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Human contract icon table; Completing contracts definitions.

answers.answer: No. If you take a board-space contract after already sending your Agent there this turn, you must wait for a future turn because you must hold it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, take its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: must hold at time of Agent placement; completion procedure.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It gets the Ornithopter Objective; humans randomly receive the other two eligible Objectives, and the human whose card shows First Player takes that marker. First Player alternates only between humans; turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. Rival takes Agent turns only and never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and Agent turns.

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type, ignore placement if none exists, and immediately reveal another card either way. Ignore ordinary space costs and effects; apply only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: skip occupied destinations; Place Spy handling; ignore normal costs/effects; reshuffle.

answers.answer: For 3–4 players, shuffle the eligible Objectives after removing cards with a mismatched 1–3P or 4/6P mark, then deal one face up to each player. The card showing the First Player marker determines the first player. Shaddam may be chosen only when using the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5: Shaddam only with CHOAM; match player-count marking, shuffle, distribute face up, marked card sets First Player.

answers.answer: The bank’s Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; make any convenient substitution if they run out. Troops are limited by a player’s supply: if it is empty, that player cannot recruit more until troops return. Payments of Solari, spice or water return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: bank resources not meant to be limited; gains from bank and payments returned; troop recruitment rule.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict from the top and place it face up beside the deck, on top of any unclaimed prior Conflict cards; then each player draws five cards. If Endgame does not trigger at Recall, humans return Agents to Leaders; with 3–4 humans pass First Player clockwise, while in 2P return Rival Agents to supply and pass the marker to the other human, then start next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phases; Round Start reveal before drawing; Recall next-round preparation.

answers.answer: Yes, you may resolve the board-space effects, played card’s Agent-box effects, and Faction Influence advance in any order. No, you must pay entry costs and meet requirements before resolving those effects, so that visit’s Influence cannot meet its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: entry cost/requirements first; then effects and Influence in any order.

answers.answer: No. An optional arrow cost/effect may be paid only once per turn; you are not forced to pay and get no effect if you decline. Most card and space effects are mandatory, except “may,” optional arrow costs and optional black-X trash; direct instruction to trash itself is mandatory. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: The Spy icon places a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post; some effects require the post be connected to a specified Agent icon, and then you cannot use another type. If you have no Spy in supply, you may first recall one of your own deployed Spies for no effect, then place it.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: unoccupied post, recall one if supply empty; specified Agent-icon connection constraint.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate bypasses only another player’s Agent, not your own. Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence recall is available without a card, but an Agent-turn card is still required to send an Agent. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you can recall one for Infiltrate and another for Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies: Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent; FAQ says card still required; may recall two for distinct effects, never two Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: When anyone visits a controlled Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, the controller gains 1 Solari; for Imperial Basin, the controller gains 1 spice. The visitor also receives the space’s own effects, including if visitor is controller. A critical-location Conflict winner replaces the prior Control marker with theirs. When a Conflict is revealed for a space already controlled, its controller may deploy 1 troop from supply directly to the Conflict, without visiting.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; Board Space Guide says resolve visitor and controller effects separately.

answers.answer: For a tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps their first reward and card, and no further rewards are given. A tie for third receives nothing. Three tied for first each get the second reward, nobody takes the card, and nobody gets other rewards, in either three- or four-player play.
answers.evidence: Combat ties and three tied for first table.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three distinct positive strengths, first and second receive their printed rewards; third receives nothing. This is the same in a two-human game with the Rival participating: 2P is treated as a three-player game for ranks, so only ordinary first and second are paid.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with 2 or 3 players ordinary first and second get rewards; ordinary third none; Rival counts in 2P.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues are playable during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues only during Combat and with at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down separate from your deck, and after resolving one put it face up in an Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue Deck runs out, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards timing and storage; FAQ Draw timing says reshuffle Intrigue discard when deck runs out.

answers.answer: No, an ordinary discard instruction means a card of your choice from your hand and not an Intrigue unless specified. The Steal Intrigue icon makes each opponent who has 4 or more Intrigues give you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Intrigue cards—Steal Intrigue icon.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from your hand, discard pile or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box; Reserve cards go back to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional except when paying a cost or told to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its acquired VP; that VP is retained.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ Victory says The Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained if card later trashed.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment you acquire the card. When a draw is needed and your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn and cannot carry over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards: reshuffle when deck empty, unused Persuasion lost.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on your Reveal turn remain face up and in play through Clean Up, unless trashed earlier. Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of which was played first. They cease to be in play when moved to discard at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed; you may use that recalled Agent on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop moves from Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” allows zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A free-choice effect granting two Influence requires both advances on one chosen Faction, not split across factions. An Alliance-icon effect requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires meeting its stated threshold.
answers.evidence: Influence: free-choice gain two cannot choose two Factions; Alliance icon/minimum requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with multiple opponents, the former holder chooses which formerly tied opponent receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board; the former holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring FAQ: if several were tied, former holder chooses recipient; at 3 or lower with nobody 4+, token returns and VP lost.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal stays for next round, when the player draws five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until then, resolves then, and is discarded afterward.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first, because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: win-Conflict Intrigue cannot be played after tie; if received as winning reward, play immediately.

answers.answer: If VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track’s 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts you hold for that same space with one Agent placement; you cannot delay completion. Contract completion is another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, but you must have held the contract when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the two set-aside Sardaukar contracts; he may choose a reserved one when acquiring a contract, and only he may acquire them. His Emperor of the Known Universe deployment restriction begins immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent, and lasts for that turn only, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM reserved contracts; FAQ Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd’s token starts on the leftmost space of his printed Training track and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications.

answers.answer: Yes: for Margot/Irulan moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2; reaching 2 again by later losing Influence and regaining it can count again. Moving down through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild’s Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade, costs nothing, always draws one card, and resolves the contract icon: without CHOAM or when all contracts are taken, gain 2 Solari; otherwise take a face-up contract and replace it. It gives no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service uses Emperor, costs nothing, gains 1 Emperor Influence (counted once), and resolves the same contract icon. As an Emperor Faction space, its visit automatically advances Emperor once; its listed influence is that same advance, not an additional one.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: shared contract rule and space rows; faction-status clarification.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits 1 troop and draws 1 card, plus controller gets 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw 1 card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit 2 troops and draw 2 cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, summons 2 sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, summons 1 sandworm. Both give all accumulated bonus spice whichever option you choose. Hooks are retained, not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows; Makers; FAQ Spies says Hooks retained, not spent.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit 1 troop and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option does not recruit a troop.
answers.evidence: Sietch Tabr row: two options and requirements.

answers.answer: High Council uses Landsraad access, costs 5 Solari each visit, and is not a Combat space. First visit places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits grant 2 spice, draw an Intrigue and recruit 3 troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—High Council.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone obtains it and 6 after anyone has one. Each player can take it only once per game. The third Agent becomes available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, and costs 3 Solari. It lets you discard an Intrigue to draw one Intrigue, then recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically grant Emperor Influence; it is a Landsraad space.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Imperial Privilege; Faction status clarification.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gains 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Shipping.

answers.answer: Gather Support is a non-Combat Landsraad space: pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit 2 troops either way, and if paying 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is a Combat City space: pay 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari for free or 4 Solari if paying 1, and its controller gets 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild, Combat yes, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits 5 troops. Desert Tactics: Fremen, Combat yes, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits 1 and may trash a card. Sardaukar: Emperor, Combat no, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits 4 troops. Only Heighliner and Desert Tactics permit normal deployment.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar; Combat column definition.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall: Landsraad, no cost, non-Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage: Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, non-Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies: Spacing Guild, no cost, non-Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes each affected opponent move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it can be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when the card gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings—False Orders and Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: No opponent may acquire the card Manipulate removed. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If still unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings—Manipulate.

answers.answer: The Rival gets a color, four Influence cubes at track bottoms, 3 troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, 2 Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, 3 Spies and 1 water; score and Combat marker start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and place it near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. Its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall like a human and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and Rival scoring.

answers.answer: As soon as its counted resources reach its printed Swordmaster value, it spends that many and takes the third Agent, usable in the current round. Count Solari, spice, Intrigues and water at 1 each; spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigues, then water. Keep leftovers. Count only Hagal/Conflict sources, not ordinary spaces or 4-Influence track bonuses (except Maker/control bonuses).
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Once it has Swordmaster, spend each set when it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, for 1 VP per set. Seven mixed resources do not form a VP set.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster: each exact set is separately named.

answers.answer: When selecting Influence, the Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains VP at 2 and gets Alliance VP/transfers like a human, but gets no resource bonus for reaching 4 (track bonus). A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that numbered position in the Rival card’s Faction-priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival influence selection and resources; Hagal numbered Influence icon description.

answers.answer: No. For a two-destination card, use only the destination selected by current conditions; if it is occupied, reveal another Hagal card, without using the other destination. Accept Contract/Shipping are selected by Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner by Conflict tier.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination card conditions and occupied behavior.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to 2 available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a non-Combat space go to its garrison. A conditional bonus at 2+ Influence that it lacks is simply omitted; it never prevents Agent placement.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop icons and Combat deployment; conditional 2+ bonus does not prevent placement.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival chooses the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. On placing its third and final supply Spy, immediately recall its other two Spies and resolve its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If its Scheme recruits troops before Agent placement and it then visits a Combat space that same turn, deploy those recruited troops too. A Place Spy card with no legal post ignores placement, then immediately reveals another Hagal card and continues the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Place Spy cards do not place an Agent.

answers.answer: The Rival always collects accumulated bonus spice. At Hagga or Deep Desert, if it has Hooks and the Conflict allows worms, it summons one or two worms respectively instead of base spice. If it summons none—because it lacks Hooks or the Conflict is protected—it takes base spice (Hagga 2, Deep Desert 4).
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords to its strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. With no unit it gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat.

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival gains control bonuses, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and sandworm reward doubling normally. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay the resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat.

answers.answer: During Reveal effects, total Combat strength, announce it and set the marker at any point while resolving, updating as needed. A Combat Intrigue may later change units/strength, requiring marker update when it resolves. At over 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again at the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn—Resolve Reveal Effects; Strength; Combat Intrigue marker update.

answers.answer: A Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal it. Card text can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader abilities; overview says cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. By itself it is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate free recall actions with their own effects.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Recall Spy icon; Spy may also be recalled without a card for two named effects.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction instead selects a card from your hand and cannot select Intrigue unless specified; it discards rather than trashes.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: Yes. Sandworm doubling allows the reward’s optional cost to be paid again for a second reward; the example allows 2 Influence with the same Faction or two different Factions. By contrast, a single free-choice effect that grants two Influence must put both on one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example; Influence free-choice icon rule.

answers.answer: Resolve the Signet Ring ability printed on the selected Rival card, not its Scheme. It is triggered by the Hagal Signet Ring effect; no human Signet Ring card or Rival Reveal turn is involved.
answers.evidence: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme table.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon takes one token if the Rival lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no extra. Shield Wall removal works only if it has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks it is ignored, and if the Wall is already gone it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, costs nothing and is non-Combat. It grants 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Secrets; Steal Intrigue rule.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, costs nothing and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice. If that same visitor controls it, the controller bonus separately adds 1 spice, so the player gains base 2 plus bonus spice total.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Imperial Basin; controlled-location effects resolve separately.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict and place it face up next to the deck on top of any cards left from earlier rounds. Those unclaimed cards remain there underneath. Players draw five cards after the Conflict reveal.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start.

answers.answer: Each of the four Faction Influence tracks starts with that Faction’s Alliance token on its marked area; each human places one cube on each track’s bottom space. No human starts holding an Alliance. The Shield Wall token is initially on its marked area below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6; Maker Hooks/Wall setup context.

answers.answer: The First Player takes the first turn and play proceeds clockwise, one turn at a time. Revealed players are skipped for the rest of Player Turns; in standard 3–4 player play, Player Turns ends when all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue begins with First Player and proceeds clockwise; an eligible player may play any number or pass. The window ends after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns order and ending; Combat Intrigue order and pass rule.

answers.answer: The steps are Reveal Cards (reveal remaining hand), Resolve Reveal Effects (resolve those cards’ Reveal boxes, spend Persuasion, total/announce/set strength), then Clean Up (move all cards in front to discard). Reveal effects may be resolved in any order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn’s three listed steps; effects in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human’s 10-card starting deck face down and put it in their supply left of Leader. Omit CHOAM-marked cards, then shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks separately and place both face down; deal 5 face-up Imperium Row cards. Put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies and Councilor token remain in the player’s supply; Control markers remain in supply, with no initial location control.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6; Initial card states table; per-player components.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, ordinarily acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards or Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow from Reserve. Its cost is shown at the card’s top right. Ordinary Persuasion purchases occur during Reveal, not an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional, even if legal. The Shield Wall detonation icon also says you may remove it. Once destroyed, the Wall is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts says placement/recall optional; Shield Wall rule says may remove and cannot return.

answers.answer: Normally the destination’s upper-left Agent icon must match an icon on the played card, and the destination must be unoccupied unless using Infiltrate. A connected Spy alone does not let a City-only card send an Agent to Shipping. If the played card has the Spy Agent icon and a Spy at a connected post, that icon permits access to the connected space.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn and Spy Agent icon rule.

answers.answer: Yes. During your Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue, and resources it grants before placement may pay the entry cost. Resources from the Agent card played to send the Agent, or from the destination, arrive after placement and cannot pay that same cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot before placement may supply entry cost; post-placement gains cannot.

answers.answer: No. In 2P, even after both humans Reveal, the Rival continues taking Agent turns while it has Agents in supply; go to Combat only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns two-player special rule.

answers.answer: When the Conflict is revealed for a location the human already controls, they may deploy one troop from supply directly to that Conflict, without an Agent visit; taking this defensive bonus is optional. After Conflict rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start defensive bonus; Critical Locations & Control; Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one of your Agents from your Leader to a matching unoccupied space. Resolve that card’s Agent box, not its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard; you cannot simply move an Agent already on the board (Recall Agent is a distinct effect returning another Agent to Leader).
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one card from hand and send Agent from Leader; resolve Agent box. Clean Up and recall rules.

answers.answer: The restriction already applies immediately when Signet Ring is played to send an Agent; resolving board-space effects first cannot delay it. The recruited troop cannot deploy that turn.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Shaddam restriction takes effect immediately; CHOAM Shaddam Signet benefits.

answers.answer: First, second and third receive the corresponding printed rewards; fourth receives no reward. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card (then checks for a battle-icon match).
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with four players ordinary top three receive rewards; winner takes Conflict card.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not mandatory.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: choose a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile; when the deck is empty, shuffle the discard pile into a new deck and draw.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. The Reshuffle card is not removed.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. When a player acquires one, move it from the bank onto that player’s garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Yes. If a Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise alters strength, update that player’s Combat marker when the card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. Rewards use the adjusted strength shown on the track, not a fixed Reveal value.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: marker update when card resolves; combat resolved using adjusted track strength.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice or water tokens come from the bank; you may not take them from another player’s supply. Payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: gain from bank, pay back to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contract tokens face down, then flip two face up on the marked board spaces and leave the other 18 face down in the bank. Offers are random; players do not choose them or preset the face-down order.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: shuffle all 20; two public offers and rest face down in bank.

answers.answer: Before the contract shuffle, set aside both Sardaukar contracts; only Shaddam may acquire them, and they do not start in his possession. Shuffle the other 18, expose 2 face-up public offers, and leave 16 face down in bank, with the two reserved contracts separate.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes and Reserved Sardaukar contracts.
